questions.audit_notes: Topic candidate legacy Q28 (Atwood machine centre-of-mass displacement); verify exact values/options.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: For the given Atwood machine, find the displacement (in m) of the centre of mass after 2 s of release. The 2 kg and 1 kg blocks start at the same horizontal level. (Take g = 10 m/s².)
draft_candidate.solution: The Atwood acceleration is a = (2−1)g/(2+1) = 10/3 m/s². Each block travels s = at²/2 = 20/3 m in opposite directions. Taking the 2 kg block's downward direction as positive, the centre-of-mass displacement is (2s−s)/3 = 20/9 m downward. Option A. Final-key confirmation remains pending.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: A hollow cylinder of radius 1 m is rotating with angular velocity ω = 10 rad/s. Find the minimum coefficient of friction μ so that a block remains at rest with respect to the cylinder.
draft_candidate.solution: The normal force supplied by the rotating cylinder is N = mω²r. For the block not to slide down, friction must balance its weight: μN ≥ mg. Thus μ_min = g/(ω²r) = 10/(10²×1) = 0.1, option A. Official final-key confirmation remains pending.

draft_candidate.question_text: An air bubble of radius 1 mm rises with constant speed 0.5 cm/s in a liquid of density 2000 kg/m³. Find the coefficient of viscosity η in poise.
draft_candidate.solution: Using Stokes' law for a small rising bubble and neglecting the bubble's density, η = 2r²ρg/(9v). With r = 1×10⁻³ m, ρ = 2000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s² and v = 5×10⁻³ m/s, η = 8/9 Pa·s = 80/9 poise, option C. Official final-key confirmation remains pending.

questions.audit_notes: Topic candidate legacy Q49 (convex lens burning paper); numerical answer and source details need verification.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: If sunlight is focused on a paper using a convex lens, it starts burning the paper in the shortest time when the lens is kept at 30 cm above the paper. If the radius of curvature of the lens is 60 cm and the refractive index of the lens material is α/10, the value of α is:
draft_candidate.solution: The sunlight is focused at the focal plane, so f=30 cm. For a symmetric thin biconvex lens with radii 60 cm, the lens-maker formula gives 1/f=(n−1)(1/60−(−1/60))=(n−1)/30. With f=30 cm, n−1=1, hence n=2 and α=20.

questions.audit_notes: Topic candidate legacy Q47 (Bohr orbit magnetic-field ratio); exact options and key pending.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: Using Bohr's model, calculate the ratio of the magnetic fields generated due to the motion of electrons in the 2nd and 4th orbits of a hydrogen atom.
draft_candidate.solution: In the Bohr model, orbital radius rₙ∝n² and orbital period Tₙ∝n³, so current Iₙ=e/Tₙ∝n⁻³. The magnetic field at the centre of a circular orbit is Bₙ=μ₀Iₙ/(2rₙ), hence Bₙ∝n⁻⁵. Therefore B₂/B₄=(4/2)⁵=32.

questions.audit_notes: Topic candidate legacy Q29 (Lorentz force/velocity); candidate text corrected; official key pending.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: A particle of charge 10⁻⁹ C moves in the x-y plane in uniform fields E⃗ = 0.4 ĵ V/m and B⃗ = 2 × 10⁻³ k̂ T. The force on the particle is F⃗ = (2 × 10⁻¹⁰ î + 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ ĵ) N. The velocity of the particle is:
draft_candidate.solution: Use F⃗ = q(E⃗ + v⃗ × B⃗). For v⃗ = vₓ î + vᵧ ĵ and B⃗ = 2×10⁻³ k̂, v⃗ × B⃗ = 2×10⁻³(vᵧ î − vₓ ĵ). The î component gives 2×10⁻¹⁰/10⁻⁹ = 2×10⁻³vᵧ, hence vᵧ = 100 m/s. The ĵ component gives 3×10⁻¹⁰/10⁻⁹ = 0.4 − 2×10⁻³vₓ, hence vₓ = 50 m/s. Therefore v⃗ = 50 î + 100 ĵ m/s, option A. Official answer-key verification remains pending.

questions.audit_notes: Corrected target to 3L₂ − L₁ and swapped switch labels in the reconstructed diagram so S₁ bypasses L₁ and S₂ bypasses L₂. Calculation gives 2/9 H; official key/source-figure check remains open.

draft_candidate.subject: Physics
draft_candidate.question_text: The figure shows an LCR series circuit with two switches S₁ and S₂. When S₁ is closed while S₂ is open, the phase difference φ between current and source voltage is 30°. When S₂ is closed while S₁ is open, the phase difference is 60°. Find (3L₂ − L₁) in henries.
draft_candidate.solution: Let X = 1/(ωC). With S₁ closed, L₁ is bypassed and L₂ remains in the circuit, so tan 30° = (ωL₂ − X)/R. With S₂ closed, L₂ is bypassed and L₁ remains, so tan 60° = (ωL₁ − X)/R. Since tan 60° = 3 tan 30°, ωL₁ − X = 3(ωL₂ − X), giving 3L₂ − L₁ = 2/(ω²C). Here ω = 300 rad/s and C = 100 μF, so the value is 2/[300² × 100 × 10⁻⁶] = 2/9 H, option B. This derivation depends on the corrected switch placement in the schematic; final answer-key confirmation remains pending.

questions.audit_notes: Topic-level candidate: source Chemistry Q2 asks osmotic pressures x, y and z for two protein solutions and their mixture; compare exact solution setup and all option values against legacy Q55.

draft_candidate.subject: Chemistry
draft_candidate.question_text: Solution A is prepared by dissolving 1 g of a protein (molar mass 50000 g mol⁻¹) in 0.5 L of water at 300 K; its osmotic pressure is x bar. Solution B is prepared by dissolving 2 g of the same protein in 1 L of water at 300 K; its osmotic pressure is y bar. The entire solution A is mixed with the entire solution B at the same temperature and the resultant osmotic pressure is z bar. Given R=0.083 L bar mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find x, y and z.
draft_candidate.solution: Osmotic pressure is π=(n/V)RT. For solution A, n=1/50000 mol and V=0.5 L, so n/V=4×10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹. For solution B, n=2/50000 mol and V=1 L, giving the same concentration. Thus x=y=(4×10⁻⁵)(0.083)(300)=9.96×10⁻⁴ bar. After mixing, total moles are 6×10⁻⁵ mol and total volume is 1.5 L, again giving 4×10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹, so z is also 9.96×10⁻⁴ bar. The source option order places this triple in option A, matching NTA final answer key option ID 691121697.

draft_candidate.subject: Chemistry
draft_candidate.question_text: Gas A undergoes a change from state X to state Y, absorbing 10 J of heat while 18 J of work is done by the gas. Gas A is brought back from Y to X by another process during which 6 J of heat is evolved. In the reverse process Y to X, which statement is correct?

draft_candidate.solution: For X→Y, ΔU=Q−W=10−18=−8 J. Hence for Y→X, ΔU=+8 J. The reverse process releases 6 J, so Q=−6 J. From ΔU=Q−W, 8=−6−W, giving W=−14 J: 14 J of work is done on the gas by the surroundings. Option D.

questions.audit_notes: Topic-level candidate: source Chemistry Q8 reaction order/rate-constant statements; compare rate constant, statements and correct combination against legacy Q57.

draft_candidate.subject: Chemistry
draft_candidate.question_text:
Consider the reaction aX → bY, for which the rate constant at 30°C is 1×10⁻³ mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹. Which of the following statements are true?
A. When the concentration of X is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes 16 times.
B. The reaction is a second order reaction.
C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X.
D. Decomposition of N₂O₅ is an example of the above reaction.
E. The graph of ln([R₀]/[R]) versus time is a straight line, as shown.
options: A, B, D and E Only
draft_candidate.solution: The units of k (mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹) indicate a second-order reaction, so rate ∝ [X]². Quadrupling [X] makes the rate 16 times larger (A true), and the reaction is second order (B true). For a second-order reaction, half-life depends on initial concentration (C false). N₂O₅ decomposition is first order (D false), and ln([R₀]/[R]) versus time is the first-order linear plot, not the second-order plot (E false). Therefore A and B only, option A; this matches the NTA final answer key.
